does: Converts a date and time in one IANA time zone to the same moment in a second IANA time zone, and gives the difference in hours between the two, from Node's own time zone data alone.

offerings.name: Convert a date and time
offerings.does: Gives the same moment as a date and time in a second IANA time zone, with the difference in hours between the two zones at that moment.

inputs.name: datetime
inputs.about: The date and time where it starts, written as 2026-11-12T09:30.

inputs.name: from
inputs.about: The time zone that date and time is in, by its IANA name, such as America/Denver.

inputs.name: to
inputs.about: The time zone to convert it to, by its IANA name, such as Europe/Paris.

outputs.name: conversion
outputs.about: A short Markdown piece: a header of the fields `from`, `to`, `datetime_from`, `datetime_to` and `difference_hours`, with `ambiguous` when the time happens twice, then one sentence saying the same in words. A refusal carries the header field `refused` and one sentence saying why.

refusals:
Accepting a time zone name that Node's own time zone data does not know, because any answer for it would be invented; it says the name is unknown, names it, and converts nothing.
Guessing a time zone from a city or country name such as Paris, France or Japan, because a city or country can span several zones; it asks for an IANA name such as Europe/Paris and converts nothing.
Converting a date and time that is not a real calendar date and clock time, such as 2026-02-30T10:00, because no moment matches it; it says so and converts nothing.
Converting a clock time that the first place skips when its clocks jump forward, because that moment never happens there; it says the time does not exist in that zone and converts nothing.
Giving a guessed time when Node's own time zone data cannot be read or fails, because a wrong time is worse than none; it says the conversion could not be made.

records.name: the signed job manifest of each delivery

can_use.does: writes the organization's name as the brand writes it, uses its first-mention form the first time, and keeps out the words the brand never says
can_use.without: writes the organization's name as the person gave it, and says that no brand profile was given

can_use.does: writes in the organization's voice, tone and spelling, and uses the words it prefers in place of the ones it avoids
can_use.without: writes in a plain, neutral voice in the spelling of the words it was given, and says that no style guide was given
